Both statements are copied into the bibliography. Short phrases only, the documents cited. The articles reprinted in the same issue, Jorgenson and Griliches (1967, from The Review of Economic Studies) and Denison (1969), are treated as in copyright: short phrases only. Rows read on page images (no quotation, the transcription between « and » in the note): Harrod's fundamental equation and his numbers (pp. 17-18), whose subscripts and fractions the text layer drops; Solow's equation (6) of 1956 (p. 69); Swan's production function (p. 334) and his rate of technical progress (p. 337); Solow (1957), pp. 312-317 and 320, whose text layer interleaves the two columns and misreads the figures; Easterly and Fischer's Tables 1 and 6 and their equation (6) (pp. 343, 356, 357); the study for the Joint Economic Committee, pp. 6-7 (the text and Table 2), whose text layer is poor; the index of Econometrica 14. Misreadings of the text layers and misprints, each as printed in the quotation: 'eight' for 'eighth' (nb_eight); 'approachindeed' for 'approach—indeed' (hr_revolution); 'equilibriumpoint' without a space (hr_point); 'ri' for 'r1' (s56_three, s56_lower); '0-4' for '0·4' (sw_alpha, sw_impact); '4 per cent' for '½ per cent' (sw_m_ocr), as the page image shows (sw_m); 'anwers' for 'answers' (sw_answers); 'AContribution' without a space (sw_solow); 'investmenetis' for 'investment is' (ph_theorem); 'dispersed,happy' without a space (ph_crowd); '87'2' for '87½' (s57_ocr), as the page image shows (s57_summary); '0.751n' for '0.75 ln' (bm_eq); 'thirtyfive' for 'thirty-five' (dl_sd); 'are are' as printed (dl_concede); 'fl' for 'β' (bs_countries); 'o' for 'α' (mrw_059); 'end' for 'and' (mrw_third, mrw_textbook); 'a-$-l/3' for 'α = β = 1/3' (mrw_lambda); '-O' for 'β = 0' (mrw_textbook); 'affects' for 'effects' (mrw_direction); 'modem' for 'modern' (pr_dominant); words run together (pr_ratio, pr_dominant, pr_compatible); 'C)' for '©' (ef_copyright); 'tp' for 'to' (ef_caveats); '1-60' and '0-10' for '1·60' and '0·10' (jg_160); '1818' for '1918' (loc_swan_born). The decimals with a raised point that the text layers read as hyphens are read by the rule 'dot' of checks/check_ch40.py, the 'l' of 'l/3' by the rule 'lfrac'. Disagreements and slips in the sources: Solow (1956, p. 85) gives the eventual growth rate of output with neutral technical change as n + ag/b and the growth of K/Y as g (s56_ag, s56_kyg); with his own production function Y = e^{gt} K^a L^b, b = 1 - a, output and capital both grow at n + g/b on the balanced path and K/Y is constant (checks/check_ch40.py). Easterly and Fischer's Table 6 labels the row c5 the elasticity of substitution and prints -0.37 (ef_t6_sigma); by their equation (6) (ef_t6_eq) the elasticity is -c5, 0.37, as their text says it is low (ef_low). Pritchett's text gives the ratio of 1985 as 51 (pr_ratio), his table 51.6 (pr_t_1985). The LoC record of Swan has '1818-01-14' in the field of the date of birth (loc_swan_born), 1918 in the heading and the source note (loc_swan, loc_swan_note). Single witnesses: Harrod's equation and numbers (hr_eq, hr_numbers); Swan's numerical example (sw_n, sw_alpha, sw_s, sw_thrift, sw_impact, sw_m); Solow's figures for 1909-1949 (s57_t1_1909, s57_t1_1949, s57_first21, s57_doubled, s57_eighth, s57_623, s57_cents, s57_avg, s57_fn6), which his lecture of 1987 repeats in round terms (nb_eight, nb_capital12); Abramovitz's index (ab_14, ab_250); Denison's decomposition of 1929-1982, only in Solow's lecture (nb_denison to nb_misc), and his figure of Why Growth Rates Differ, only in his article of 1969 (dn_137); Baumol's and De Long's regressions (bm_eq, dl_sd); the estimates of Barro and Sala-i-Martin and of Mankiw, Romer and Weil (bs_states, bs_alpha, mrw_059, mrw_80, mrw_lambda); Pritchett's ratios (pr_ratio, pr_sixfold); Easterly and Fischer's Table 1, which cites Gomulka and Schaffer (1991) (ef_t1_source), and their Table 6; the estimates of Soviet GNP in 1982 prices (jec_t2_gnp, jec_t2_cons, jec_t2_inv, jec_percapita). The reduction of total factor productivity growth by Jorgenson and Griliches has two witnesses, their article (jg_160) and Denison's (dn_010); they agree. Indirect testimony: Solow's lecture on Harrod, Domar and Lewis (nb_trail, nb_routes) and on Denison (nb_heldup to nb_misc); Swan on Joan Robinson (sw_robinson_fn, sw_units, sw_scarecrow); Solow (1957) on Joan Robinson (s57_robinson), on Kendrick's and Goldsmith's series (s57_data, s57_goldsmith) and on Fabricant (s57_fabricant); De Long on Maddison (1982) (dl_design); Easterly and Fischer on Ofer (1987) (ef_extensive), on the Kaldor stylized fact (ef_kaldor, ef_contradicts), on Weitzman (1970, 1990) (ef_weitzman, ef_best), on Bergson (1983) (ef_bergson), on Krugman (1994) (ef_krugman) and on Khanin's data (ef_khanin); the BEA's introduction on the reply of Jorgenson and Griliches (scb_reply). Not obtained: Domar (1946) itself: only the index of Econometrica 14 (dm_index); Weitzman (1970): the working paper on Yale University's site sits behind a Cloudflare challenge, not tried; Kaldor's statement of the stylized facts; Ofer (1987); Pritchett's article in The Journal of Economic Perspectives (1997): the site refused access; Denison, Why Growth Rates Differ (1967); the pages of the CIA's reading room, which did not open. Life dates: Swan, Denison, Griliches, Lewis and Robinson from the headings of the Library of Congress (loc_swan, loc_denison, loc_griliches, loc_lewis, loc_robinson); the GND agrees where it has the years (gnd_swan_born, gnd_swan_died, gnd_denison_born, gnd_griliches_born, gnd_griliches_died, gnd_lewis_born, gnd_lewis_died, gnd_robinson_born, gnd_robinson_died). Solow: the LoC heading has no years; the record's source notes give the date of birth (loc_solow_born) and of death (loc_solow_died, loc_solow_wapo), as NobelPrize.org (nf_born, nf_died) and the GND (gnd_solow_born, gnd_solow_died) do. Abramovitz: the heading has no years; the source note gives them (loc_abramovitz_note), as the GND does (gnd_abramovitz_born, gnd_abramovitz_died). Phelps: the heading has no years; the source note gives the date of birth (loc_phelps_born); the date of death from the GND (gnd_phelps_died) and NobelPrize.org (nf_phelps_died), which agree, as they do on the date of birth (gnd_phelps_born, nf_phelps_born). Harrod, Domar and Jorgenson: the records of Chapters 33, 34 and 39 (islm_facts, warfinance_facts, consumption_facts).
